data.name: Bhoomi
data.gender_notes: Bhoomi is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Bhoomi is the goddess of the Earth, who is the wife of Vishnu and the mother of all beings. She is the source of all life and the giver of sustenance. Bhoomi is also known as Prithvi and is one of the primary deities in Hinduism. The name Bhoomi carries the meaning “Earth, ground, or land” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Bhoomi usually hope their child will grow to embody earth, ground, or land and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the stability, nurturing, and grounding energy of the Earth.
data.etymology: Bhoomi belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Earth, ground, or land.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bhoomi total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Bhoomi" holds great cultural significance in Hinduism, as it represents the goddess of the Earth. Bhoomi is often invoked during rituals and prayers, seeking her blessings for fertility, prosperity, and protection. In various Hindu texts and epics, Bhoomi is portrayed as a nurturing mother, providing sustenance to all life forms.
data.spiritual_significance: Bhoomi signifies our connection to the Earth and the Cosmos. As per Hindu beliefs, the Earth is not merely a physical entity but a living being, nurturing and providing for all life forms. By spiritualizing the name "Bhoomi," one can develop an appreciation for the Earth and its role in our lives, fostering a sense of gratitude, respect, and stewardship towards the natural world.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Bhoomi, the earth goddess, nurtures life with her fertile soil. She embodies the primal, maternal force that sustains all living beings. Her name, derived from the Sanskrit word for earth, is a reminder of our deep connection to the earth and the natural world.
